transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah. Hi. I'm just here because... well, it's mostly at night. When I'm alone. I just, um... I start eating and then it's like I can't stop. Even when I know I should, or I'm telling myself to just put it away, I just... I don't know, it feels like I lose control.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise a lot to try to control your weight or shape?
Um... yeah. I mean, after I eat like that... I usually end up in the bathroom. I just... I make myself throw up. It just feels like the only way to undo it, I guess. Before the calories settle in.
How often do these episodes of eating and making yourself vomit happen? Are they happening regularly, like several times a week?

Um... yeah, I guess. It's been going on for a while. Maybe like... the last four months? Usually, it's at least one night a week where I just... eat way more than I meant to when I'm by myself. And then... yeah. I throw up after.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting) occurring at least once a week over a four-month period. This meets the criteria for bulimia nervosa. Anorexia nervosa, binge-eating/purging type, is ruled out as the patient does not report significant weight loss, fear of gaining weight, or body image disturbance as the primary driver of the behavior.
